answer: Reputation Decay Pricing. Each new identity pays a fee that rises with the umber of identities already derived from the same funding source, priced on a steepening curve. An agent's standing decays without a pulse of verified activity, so dormant sybils lose weight. Every voyage into a new identity resets earned history at a compounding premium, making a thousand-identity fleet cost superlinearly more than one. The attacker's per-identity cost grows faster than the count, capping marginal returns.
